## Preliminary Work

The steps below are preliminary work you will need to complete before you can complete the actual assignment.
You will not be able to complete the assignment withtout them, but you do not need to document them in your HW_01 notebook.

### Step 1: Set up your course repository

1. On GitHub.com, create a new private repository where you will share all of your work for this class with me.
2. Clone the repository to your computer.
3. Fill out this [form](https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeGFGaIWcfXhtonaRaJPJwSGkUsFW429lkeWerNxy71ZSkzJQ/viewform?usp=publish-editor) to share the repository with me. The URL should be how you navigate to your repository in a browser (e.g., https://github.com/gabehassler/RGS-Intro-to-Machine-Learning). It should not end in `.git`.
4. Add me @gabehassler as a collaborator on the project.

### Step 2: Set up the Census API Key
You will be donwloading data from the US Census API.

1. Request the key [here](https://api.census.gov/data/key_signup.html).

2. Create a `.env` file at the root of your git repo and add  *environment variable* API key. The file should look like:

```{shell}
CENSUS_API_KEY=<YOUR API KEY>
```

3. Add the `.env` file to your `.gitignore`. Make sure that it is not being tracked by git.

### Step 3: Set up the python virtual environment

1. Copy the `requirements.txt` file from this repository to the root of your repository.
2. Create the virtual environment by running `python -m venv .venv` or `python3 -m venv .venv`.
3. Activate the python environment. On a Mac, use `source .venv/bin/activate`. On a PC, use `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` or `.\.venv\Scripts\activate.bat` depending on whether you're using PowerShell or the Command Prompt. If successful, you should see a `(.venv)` appear to the left of your terminal line.
4. Run `pip install -r requirements.txt`. This will install some of the packages you will need for this assignment.

### Step 4: Download and process the data

I've written scripts to do this for you.

1. Create a `code` directory in your repository. Copy all the scripts on the `code` directory of this repository to your repository.
2. Run each numbered script in sequential order. You can do this in either the terminal or VSCode. From the terminal, type, `python code/<script_name>.py`. In VSCode, you can also hit the "play" symbol when a file is open in the editor. The download script will take a while.
3. add the `data` folder to your .gitignore. You do not want to commit any data.

### Step 5: Basic Descriptive Statistics

1. Create a notebook file (e.g., Jupyter, Quarto). All the steps below should be completed in this document (code, results, explanation). Do not write explanations in code comments.
2. Create a table that shows the mean and standard deviation for each numeric variable across all three datasets (tract-level, county-level, and PUMA-level).
3. Answer the following questions:
   1. Describe the general pattern in the mean values across the three datasets. Are the means the same across each level of aggregation (tract, county , PUMA)? Why is this the case?
   2. Are the standard deviations the same across each level or aggregation? Why is this the case?
